newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO makes arrests over prisoner's death.
newsitem.headline: PLO makes arrests over prisoner's death.

text.p: Palestinian police have detained at least two senior PLO officials for questioning about an Arab prisoner who died while being interrogated last month, Attorney-General Khaled al-Qidra said on Tuesday.

Qidra said "six or seven people" were in detention and confirmed Palestinian newspaper reports that Hani Ayyad, chief of military intelligence in Nablus, and the West Bank town's deputy governor Abdel-Mu'ti al-Sadeq were among them.
Yousef al-Baba, a 32-year-old Palestinian resident of Nablus, died in a town lock-up while being questioned by military intelligence officers on January 31.
Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen has said that Baba was arrested without a warrant for questioning about non-security related crimes.
Qidra told Reuters that some of the suspects were detained immediately after Baba's death, while others were arrested in the last few days. He said the investigation was in an advanced stage.

Human rights organisations say about 12 Palestinians have died in detention since the Palestinian Authority took charge of parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip in 1994 under a self-rule deal with Israel.
Qidra said the Palestinian Authority does not allow torture in jail and that anyone who contravenes regulations is prosecuted and punished.
"We implement the law to the letter and we never shy from taking action against any violator of the law," he said.
